key_insight: The paper finds that long-context LLMs often waste reasoning on repetitive copying from the prompt, and that rewarding grounding in key evidence can improve both accuracy and reasoning quality.
clinical_relevance: For clinical NLP tasks with long documents, better evidence grounding may help models use chart notes or literature more reliably instead of echoing irrelevant text.
method: Built GEAR, a reward-shaping approach that adds a grounding reward for overlap with key evidence and a penalty for overlap with distractor context.
Created an automated pipeline to generate evidence-annotated training data from natural-language documents.
Tested the approach across multiple model scales and benchmarks to compare against standard accuracy-only RL.
evidence_signal: Across multiple benchmarks and model sizes, GEAR improved performance by up to +4.6 average points, with larger gains at longer contexts, while also reducing repetitive copying and thinking length.
watch_item: The evidence-annotation pipeline and grounding signals may be harder to define robustly in real clinical documents, where relevant evidence can be ambiguous or incomplete.
paper_title: Copy Less, Ground More: Overcoming Repetitive Copying in Long-Context Reasoning via Evidence-Aware Reinforcement Learning
